category_title: Female students who use silence as a mode of active listening
minimal_context: The student is practicing her group's presentation on domestic violence and traditional gender roles.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Let's practice your group's presentation on domestic violence. We need to go over your critique of the problem and your suggestions for remediation.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: I don’t understand how this can happen, how you can have such a big problem with domestic violence in today’s society!

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: What else were you going to say about that part?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: But … that’s the way it is. I know we are supposed to critique it, but I forgave my dad for what he did to us. I guess I'm just a hypocrite.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Okay, let's move on to the next section where you critique traditional gender roles.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: Well, the woman is expected to tend the home while the man is expected to be the breadwinner. But... personally, I want to be a homemaker, but that’s because I want my kids to turn out o.k., and someone has to be home with them. If you’re both working, it’s just like .... (trails off into silence)

task.content: Presenting a critique of the problem (domestic violence) and suggestions for its remediation, and critiquing traditional gender roles

context.environment: Classroom discussions and presentations over the spring semester of 2008

challenging_behavior_trigger.condition: When presumptively ‘appropriate’ conversational topics and critiques incurred dissonance with the intimacies of students’ personal and familial lives or cultural mores
challenging_behavior_trigger.observable_behavior: Said forcefully, ‘I don’t understand how this can happen...’ then trailed off: ‘But … that’s the way it is.’ Also offered an incisive critique of traditional gender roles, immediately added, ‘Personally, I want to be a homemaker...’ and trailed off again.
challenging_behavior_trigger.internal_state: Navigating apparent contradictions to maintain allegiance to their families and culture(s) while also moving through processes of conscientización
related_quotes: I don’t understand how this can happen, how you can have such a big problem [with domestic violence in today’s society]!
But … that’s the way it is.
Personally, I want to be a homemaker, but that’s because I want my kids to turn out o.k., and someone has to be home with them.

behavior_patterns.condition: When delivering thoughts and critiques in the more intimate settings of project groups
behavior_patterns.observable_behavior: Calling herself a ‘hypocrite’ when describing this situation
behavior_patterns.internal_state: Difficulty of living with a father who was threatening and abusive to her and her mother, but because she loved her father, she ‘forgave’ him
